metadata.short_desc: See whether the prefix was rewritten each turn, and compress context on demand
metadata.desc: A read-only-observation plus optional-compression dashboard for context cost: it captures the fully assembled final request, tells whether a turn only appended or rewrote the prefix, and turns provider usage into hit rate, miss-per-turn and break attribution. Observe by default; not a single byte is changed.

enabled.description: Master switch. Keep it on when you first install the plugin and want to see whether prefix caching really hits; turn it off for zero overhead (hooks return immediately).
enabled.hint: When off: no stats, no warnings, no event log.

mode.description: Run mode. When to switch to guard: only after you have read the dashboard and confirmed that an oversized history is the main reason for a low hit rate. observe is strongly recommended by default.
mode.hint: guard rewrites context; see the README's compression section — a rewrite may cost the cache hit of one request.
subtitles: Read-only: not a single byte is changed (recommended)
Lets the compressions below rewrite history, which may cost a cache hit

max_tail_chars.description: Character budget for tail injection (extra_user_content_parts). Exceeding it only warns, never rewrites. When to tune: if tail-cause breaks are frequent and miss-per-turn is high, lower it to check whether the tail itself is too long. 0 = no check.

max_context_chars.description: Character budget for the whole conversation history. Exceeding it only warns, never rewrites. When to enable: set a target (e.g. 200000) to quantify how long your history really is; the dashboard reports budget warnings. 0 = no check.

compress_tool_results.description: Compression 1: tool-result trimming. When to enable: when some plugin dumps huge tool output (web pages, file contents, logs) into the history and those results are no longer referenced. Off by default — rewriting a message mid-history makes everything after it re-bill.
compress_tool_results.hint: Hit rate may dip at first; reconcile with the dashboard's break-vs-clean and chars-saved figures.

compress_tool_keep_recent.description: How many recent tool results keep their raw text, so the model does not get a summary exactly when it needs the content. When to raise: tasks where the model re-reads recent tool output — try 3-5.

compress_tool_preview_chars.description: Characters of the tool result's first line kept after trimming. When to raise: the first line carries the key conclusion (e.g. a command's output) — try 200-500.

compress_oversize.description: Compression 2: oversize single-message trimming. When to enable: single messages of tens of thousands of characters (long documents, pasted logs, full OCR text) that are no longer in the recent turns. Off by default; it also rewrites history.
compress_oversize.hint: Head and tail are kept, the middle is elided; the same message is trimmed the same way every turn, so the cache is not broken repeatedly.

compress_max_msg_chars.description: Only messages longer than this are trimmed. When to lower: many 10k-20k-character messages sit mid-history and the dashboard shows frequent history breaks — try 8000.

compress_keep_head_chars.description: Characters kept from the head of a trimmed message (where conclusions and definitions usually are). Raise it when the head of the trimmed message is the important context.

compress_keep_tail_chars.description: Characters kept from the tail of a trimmed message (where questions and follow-ups usually are).

compress_keep_recent_msgs.description: The most recent N messages are never trimmed, keeping the conversation the model currently cares about intact. When to raise: multi-turn follow-up tasks where the model looks further back — try 4-6.

compress_archive.description: Whether trimmed-away raw text is archived inside the plugin's own data directory, so nothing is lost and you can verify later. When to turn off: you do not need the raw text or disk is tight; the replacement marker then omits the archive path.
compress_archive.hint: Archives stay inside the plugin data directory and stop being written once the archive cap is reached.

log_events.description: Write each request's observation to a local JSONL file inside the plugin data directory. When to turn off: disk is tight or you do not need past events; the dashboard still shows in-memory stats for this run.

warn_on_break.description: Log a message when a prefix break or a budget overflow is detected, so you spot the culprit in the logs. When to turn off: breaks are frequent and the log gets noisy; dashboard stats are unaffected.

defer_to.description: Yield list: when these plugins are installed, this plugin only observes and says so on the dashboard instead of compressing a second time. When to edit: add another context plugin you also run (e.g. astrbot_plugin_context_slim); an empty list means never yield.
